awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports the 19th Graduate Climate Conference (GCC), planned for 7-9 November 2025 at the Marine Biological Laboratory at Woods Hole, Massachusetts. The GCC is an interdisciplinary climate conference organized entirely by and for graduate students. It provides a discussion forum for students conducting research on climate in a variety of disciplines including atmospheric and oceanic dynamics, biogeochemical cycles, clouds and aerosols, and the cryosphere. The meeting is intended to help students familiarize themselves with the breadth of climate science, gain exposure to the enormous range of tools available to address climate-related questions, and understand how their research fits into the broader landscape of current climate science. The conference seeks to better prepare graduate students for scientific inquiry in a field that increasingly demands interdisciplinary approaches. Funds provided here support travel and subsistence for 120 students chosen through a competitive process.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The 19th annual Graduate Climate Conference, a conference run entirely by graduate students for graduate students in the climate sciences and related fields, was held on November 7 – 9, 2025 at the Marine Biological Laboratory in Woods Hole, MA. The goal of the GCC is to provide a forum for fostering connections among early career climate scientists that will lead to cross-disciplinary and cross-institutional collaborations to advance knowledge in the climate sciences. 104 participants from over 40 different subject areas and 49 institutions in the U.S. and abroad attended the GCC in 2025.

The conference featured sessions on a range of topics:

Poster sessions:

  • Coastal Dynamics
  • Sensing and Quantifying Air Pollution
  • Atmospheric Dynamics
  • Ice Dynamics
  • Fisheries and Wildlife Management
  • Risk Assessment
  • Public Policy
  • Paleoclimate
  • Living Earth’s Response to Climate Change
  • Monitoring the Oceans
  • Heat in the Ocean
  • Forecasting Climate
  • GHG and Pollution Mitigation
  • Biological Oceanography
  • Hydrology

Oral Sessions:

  • Life at the interface: Biology x Climate
  • Big Data in Climate Modeling
  • Ground up Connections: Soil, Moisture, and Temperature Feedbacks
  • Humans at the Fore: Carbon Removal, Mitigation, and Adaptation
  • Human-Climate Interactions and Hazards

Lightning Sessions:

  • Climate Change meets People and Politics
  • Managing Climate Change
  • Monitoring and Predicting Climate Change

The conference was structured so that all attendees could attend every talk and poster session, allowing them to grow acquainted with the breadth and interdisciplinarity of climate science. The conference also featured community partner workshops on Pathways to Professional Science and Introduction to Data Analysis in Python for Earth Science, as well as participant-led workshops on Bridging Climate Science and Community Outreach: Effective Communication Strategies for Graduate Researchers and conducting research on a small budget. Support from the National Science Foundation and other sponsors covered the venue charges and local costs for 104 participants, and provided travel grants to 44 of them, broadening the participation of the conference.
